steps.description: Convert "a+b*(c^d-e)^(f+g*h)-i". Operands go straight to the output; operators wait on the stack until everything that binds at least as tightly has already been written.
'a' is an operand. Its position in the output is already settled, so append it immediately.
Push '+'. It waits until something binding less tightly arrives, or the expression ends.
'b' is an operand. Its position in the output is already settled, so append it immediately.
Push '*'. It waits until something binding less tightly arrives, or the expression ends.
'(' opens a group. Push it as a floor — nothing below it may be popped until the matching ')' arrives.
'c' is an operand. Its position in the output is already settled, so append it immediately.
Push '^'. It waits until something binding less tightly arrives, or the expression ends.
'd' is an operand. Its position in the output is already settled, so append it immediately.
'^' is on the stack and binds tighter than '-', so its operands are already complete — write it out before '-' goes on.
Push '-'. It waits until something binding less tightly arrives, or the expression ends.
'e' is an operand. Its position in the output is already settled, so append it immediately.
')' closes the group: '-' belongs inside it, so it comes off now, ahead of anything outside the brackets.
Push '^'. It waits until something binding less tightly arrives, or the expression ends.
'(' opens a group. Push it as a floor — nothing below it may be popped until the matching ')' arrives.
'f' is an operand. Its position in the output is already settled, so append it immediately.
Push '+'. It waits until something binding less tightly arrives, or the expression ends.
'g' is an operand. Its position in the output is already settled, so append it immediately.
Push '*'. It waits until something binding less tightly arrives, or the expression ends.
'h' is an operand. Its position in the output is already settled, so append it immediately.
')' closes the group: '*' belongs inside it, so it comes off now, ahead of anything outside the brackets.
')' closes the group: '+' belongs inside it, so it comes off now, ahead of anything outside the brackets.
'^' is on the stack and binds tighter than '-', so its operands are already complete — write it out before '-' goes on.
'*' is on the stack and binds tighter than '-', so its operands are already complete — write it out before '-' goes on.
'+' is on the stack and binds as tightly as (and left to right, so first before) '-', so its operands are already complete — write it out before '-' goes on.
Push '-'. It waits until something binding less tightly arrives, or the expression ends.
'i' is an operand. Its position in the output is already settled, so append it immediately.
The expression is finished, so every operator still waiting is complete. Write '-' out.
Postfix form of "a+b*(c^d-e)^(f+g*h)-i" is "abcd^e-fgh*+^*+i-" — no brackets needed; the order alone records the grouping.
